findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, discarding recorded log calls
findings.body: LoggerMiddleware now logs through `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()`, a new instance, instead of the receiver. The `Info` call lands on a throwaway object, so `InfoLogs.Calls`, `Message` and `Ctx` on the logger a test injected stay empty. Any test that injects a `TestLogger` into `NewLoggerMiddleware` and asserts on its logs will see nothing. The fake should return `f` (or share its log state) so that assertions on the injected logger work.

findings.title: No tests for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware or the changed LoggerMiddleware
findings.body: The contextual-logger logic moved out of the metrics middleware into this new middleware, and LoggerMiddleware dropped its manual pluginId/endpoint/dsName/dsUID/uname/traceID params in favour of `logger.FromContext(ctx)`. The only test change is a rename in the metrics test. Nothing verifies that `instrumentContext` attaches the expected attributes for each endpoint. Nothing verifies that the logger middleware still emits those fields, including the traceID it used to add explicitly, or that the middleware ordering works. A regression in the log fields of 'Plugin Request Completed' would go unnoticed.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to the exported Logger interface breaks other implementers
findings.body: `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger` is added to the exported `plog.Logger` interface. Any other implementation of this interface outside the two updated here (`grafanaInfraLogWrapper` and `TestLogger`), such as test fakes in other packages or downstream/enterprise code, will fail to compile. This is a breaking contract change that the PR description (a rename and move) does not mention.

findings.title: FromContext silently drops contextual attributes if the assertion fails
findings.body: If `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` returns anything other than `*log.ConcreteLogger`, the code falls back to `d.New()`. That logger has none of the request's contextual attributes (pluginId, endpoint, dsUID, traceID, etc.), and nothing signals that they were lost. The middleware would then emit 'Plugin Request Completed' without the fields that were previously always added explicitly. The wrapper holds a `*ConcreteLogger` and relies on a type assertion on an interface return, which is fragile. The fallback at least deserves a comment or a test.
